Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

spDBL (development version)

New features

  • calibration_predict() gains sites, to predict at grid sites without field observations. For each posterior draw it draws the emulator field, the discrepancy and new field observations there, at the observation times, conditional on that draw’s field and discrepancy at the observed sites. The field uses the mean and covariance that calibration uses, design-row term included; the discrepancy uses the rows of U for the sites and a prior for its starting value there (m0_sites, M0_sites). joint = TRUE draws the sites jointly, for sums or maps over sites; the default draws each site from its own predictive distribution. Results at the observed sites are unchanged. New times are not supported.
  • calibration_predict() also predicts at points off the emulator grid (coords, in grid coordinates). The emulator field at a point is that of its containing cell (field = "cell", exact for cell-average simulators such as gen_pde()) or the bilinear interpolation of the four surrounding cell centres (field = "bilinear"); the discrepancy is predicted at the point itself from discrepancy_kernel, the covariance function behind U, which must reproduce U at the observed sites. Calibration objects now keep the grid coordinates.

spDBL 1.2.0

CRAN release: 2026-11-16

Changes that affect existing code or results

  • The default autoregressive designs are now causal and deterministic. A lag that does not exist yet is a column of ones (a per-site intercept), so the AR(1) design at t = 1 is no longer the response itself, and the AR(2) designs at t = 1, 2 no longer use random noise or the future value Y_3. emulator_learn() and emulator_predict() results change, and predictions no longer draw from the session’s random numbers. AR(2) emulators no longer need three time steps.
  • The design GP that predicts autoregressive design rows at untried inputs (calibration_prepare()) now uses a Matern 5/2 kernel with separate hyperparameters for each time step, instead of one squared-exponential kernel for all times. With 40 training and 50 held-out SIR runs on 10 x 10, 20 x 20 and 50 x 50 grids, the RMSE of PDE-free predictions fell by 4.0%, 9.5% and 5.2% in the first E2 benchmark profile (unit grid cells, one design; benchmarks/results/e2/paper) and by 27%, 13% and 9% on a second, independent simulation; in that profile, 95% intervals covered 95-96% of held-out values (93-95% before). Fitting one GP per time step adds about 8 s to calibration_prepare() for 26 time steps. New arguments design_kernel and design_groups select the design GP; design_kernel = "sqexp", design_groups = "shared" restores the previous one. Both Stan programs evaluate the chosen kernel, with one design variance factor per time step.
  • calibration_fit() starts the chains at the posterior mode by default (init = "mode"): in each conditional fit it runs L-BFGS from mode_starts
    1. random starts and starts every chain, slightly jittered, at the optimum with the highest log posterior density. In the E3 calibration benchmark, chains started at random settled in local modes 35 to 586 log-density units below the main mode, which carry negligible posterior mass but made the pooled draws unreliable. init = "random" and init = "midpoint" (the previous default; in the bundled dt_calibration example the midpoint equals the true parameter value) remain available. The recorded vignette example and the installed reproduction script pass init = "midpoint" and are unchanged.
  • The convergence diagnostics of calibration_fit() (diagnostics[[j]]$summary, max_rhat, min_n_eff, and summary()) are now the rank-normalised split Rhat and bulk effective sample size of Vehtari et al. (2021), from rstan::Rhat() and rstan::ess_bulk(), instead of the classic diagnostics of rstan::summary(); the tail effective sample size is added (min_ess_tail). They flag poorly mixed chains more reliably, so some fits that passed before now warn.
  • calibration_fit() requires iter. For inference use several chains and enough iterations (for example chains = 4, iter = 2000); iter = 1 is a quick execution check.
  • emulator_learn() no longer builds the dense S x S R_field unless it is supplied, so setup$R_field is NULL by default. Calibration builds the same kernel at the observed sites when it needs it, and results are unchanged. This removes an O(S^3) step and O(S^2) memory from every fit.
  • The nine helpers from the original research code (update_y_eta(), update_y_eta_one(), update_muSigma_eta_one(), sample_y_eta_one(), cal_Bt_bt(), scale_uniform(), scale_back_uniform(), expit(), cal_jacobian_logit_uniform()) are deprecated. They still work and warn once per session; options(spDBL.warn_deprecated = FALSE) silences them.
  • gen_ran_matrix() now scales by the largest absolute entry, so its entries stay in [-1, 1] as documented.

Calibration uncertainty

  • Calibration intervals were too narrow because the predictive variance of the design-row GP was never used. calibration_prepare() now propagates it by default (design_uncertainty = TRUE): at each time the field covariance gains the design GP’s error through each coefficient draw, including the correlation between design columns and between spatial blocks. Both Stan programs, the R reference densities, calibration_fit() and calibration_predict() use it. Predicting held-out runs of a 20 x 20 SIR model, pointwise 95% intervals covered 54% of outputs before and 94% after. design_uncertainty = FALSE restores the 1.1.1 behaviour, and objects prepared by 1.1.1 keep it. The recorded result in vignette("calibration") was regenerated. Design-row errors are still treated as independent across times (see vignette("calibration-details")).

New features

  • predict() for fitted emulators and prepared calibration objects gains interval = "prediction" and level. It returns pointwise predictive means, standard deviations and central intervals: Student-t given known autoregressive rows, and, for prediction without simulator runs, the equal-weight mixture over emulator draws (with the design-GP variance) summarised by its moments. Tests compare it with Monte Carlo from the package’s samplers. The benchmarks now use it.
  • Out-of-core smoothing and prediction: BS_bigdata_R() runs the backward pass over the files written by FF_bigdata_R(), and FFBS_predict_bigdata_R() predicts at new inputs block by block. Both match the in-memory BS() and FFBS_predict_exact(). FF_bigdata_R() now checks the design file’s width to find lag-2 columns instead of silently ignoring read errors.
  • print(), summary() and predict() methods for fitted emulators. The summary reports the in-sample fit of the smoothed coefficients and the posterior mean residual variance. Prepared calibration objects gain print() and predict().
  • calibration_fit(checkpoint_dir = ) now resumes: a conditional fit already saved there with the same data, settings, seed and Stan program is reused instead of refitted, so an interrupted calibration continues where it stopped. Fits saved with other settings are refitted.
  • emulator_learn(keep_draws = FALSE) (and the same argument of FFBS_sampling() and FFBS_sampling_sigma2R()) stores, instead of every episode’s coefficient draws, where each episode’s draws start in the random-number stream, and regenerates identical draws when prediction or calibration needs them. On a 20 x 20 grid with 20 draws the emulator shrinks from 197 to 71 MB, the prepared calibration input from 152 to 45 MB, and the peak memory of fitting halves; simulator-free prediction takes 3.1 s instead of 1.9 s for 50 inputs. All results are identical to stored draws. Marginal sampling only; joint draws are always stored.
  • calibration_fit(parallel_draws = ) runs that many conditional fits (one per emulator draw) at the same time in forked processes (Linux and macOS), so wall time falls roughly in proportion on machines with spare cores. Each forked fit runs its chains one after another, so parallel_draws processes run at once. With a multithreaded BLAS (oneMKL, OpenBLAS), start R with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1: forked processes can otherwise hang on the BLAS thread pool, and calibration_fit() warns when it detects this setup. Results are identical to running the fits one after another: each fit draws all its random numbers from its own seeds, and rstan’s draws do not depend on the number of cores. Convergence warnings are raised after all fits finish.
  • calibration_fit(init = ) sets the chains’ starting values: "mode" (the new default, see above), "random" (uniform within the bounds, reproducible from seed), "midpoint", or a vector of parameter values.
  • Every exported function now has a runnable example. The calibration examples that compile Stan run only interactively.
  • Fitted emulators (setup$seed, setup$spDBL_version), prepared calibration objects (seed, spDBL_version) and calibration fits (settings$spDBL_version, with settings$seed) record the seed and the spDBL version that produced them.

Bug fixes

  • prepare_data() keeps a one-row matrix when only one run goes to the training or test set, and stops with a clear message if prop_train leaves either set empty.
  • The discount factor delta was accepted but ignored by the filters, smoothers and predictors. Values other than 1 now give a warning; results are unchanged. (The samplers already required delta = 1.)
  • generate.grid.rowsnake() and generate.grid.lr() returned overlapping blocks when the grid had a single block, and left rows uncovered when the blocks spanned the full width. They now compute each block directly; the output is unchanged wherever it was a valid partition, including the calls made by emulator_learn() and emulator_predict().
  • verbose = TRUE no longer fails on short series: FF() with one time step, FF_sigma2R() and FF_I() with fewer than five, and FFBS_sampling_I() with fewer than three.
  • FFBS_sampling_I() no longer reads past the end of a time-varying G_ls list. It never used G_ls, F_ls or delta; they are kept for compatibility. It also handles a single coefficient row or column.
  • gen_pde() sizes the ODE solver’s work array by grid size instead of requesting a fixed 1.6 GB. Results are identical.
  • gen_Jt() no longer adds the nugget to the cross-covariance when a new input equals a training input.
  • update_y_eta(), update_y_eta_one() and update_muSigma_eta_one() use the input-GP prior variance gp_sigma2 + gp_tau2, not 1, so the predictive variance cannot go negative near a training input. update_muSigma_eta_one() uses the selected variance draw, like update_y_eta_one().
  • cal_jacobian_logit_uniform() skips fixed coordinates (equal bounds) rather than coordinates equal to zero.

Other changes

  • Fewer hard dependencies. ggplot2, ggpubr and scales move from Imports to Suggests: they are needed only by the plotting helpers (quick_heat(), quick_save(), plot_panel_heatmap_9() and its variants), which now say which package to install. deSolve and ReacTran also move to Suggests: only the demonstration SIR simulator (SIR(), gen_pde()) uses them. magrittr, invgamma, LaplacesDemon and matrixcalc are no longer used; their inverse-gamma draws, traces, log determinants and positive-definiteness check are computed in base R with the same definitions, so results are unchanged.
  • Calibration gradients are about 30% faster: the Kalman filter in the Stan program forms the filtered covariance with crossprod() (symmetric by construction, so the explicit re-symmetrising copy is gone) and adds the noise with add_diag(), and the programs are compiled with stanc’s O1 optimisations. Log densities and gradients agree with the previous program to 1e-12. Cached models from earlier versions are recompiled once.
  • Simulator-free prediction intervals (predict(cal, newdata, interval = "prediction")) are about 40 times faster: the design-GP rows and input-GP terms are computed once per new input and the coefficient terms once per emulator draw, instead of once per input and draw. On a 20 x 20 grid with 20 emulator draws, 50 new inputs take 1.9 s instead of 74 s. Results are unchanged (to 1e-14). recover_from_EP_exact() with block_cols binds episode blocks directly instead of through a data frame, which also speeds up predict_calibration() and calibration_validate().
  • emulator_predict() on a prepared calibration object and calibration_validate() loop over coefficient draws first, which reuses each draw’s cached residual weights. Results are identical.

Infrastructure

  • Test coverage rises from 31% to 99.9% of R and C++ lines (covr). New tests check the filters, smoothers, samplers, log predictive densities, out-of-core filtering, grid utilities, plotting, legacy helpers, and the calibration back end against independent calculations. The RStan back-end logic is also tested with a fake rstan, so it runs without compiling Stan. Suggests now requires testthat >= 3.3.2.
  • Every hand-written source file, including the vignettes, now carries an MIT license header (SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT), checked in CI.
  • citation("spDBL") also cites the software itself.
  • GitHub Actions: R CMD check on macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu (R devel, release, previous release); test coverage including the RStan integration tests; license-header check; pkgdown website.
  • New pkgdown website with a grouped function reference and an architecture article for contributors.
  • New contributing guide, code of conduct, and issue and pull request templates.
  • README: CRAN installation, a runnable quick example, and documentation links.

spDBL 1.1.2

  • Add analytical and draw-based WAIC for independent-row multivariate regression, with pointwise scores, optional log likelihoods for loo, input validation, and a self-contained model-comparison vignette.

spDBL 1.1.1

CRAN release: 2026-10-29

  • Calibration accepts a positive-definite discrepancy covariance scale U with non-unit diagonal, preserving the original research experiment’s discrepancy-to-observation variance ratio.

  • Default emulator coefficient sampling to smoothed marginals conditional on a shared covariance draw. Add sampling = “joint” for coherent backward paths under both scalar-variance and inverse-Wishart covariance models.

  • Let calibration preparation inherit or explicitly change the fitted sampling method, with sampling metadata retained in saved objects and fit summaries.

  • Default calibration to one chain, one iteration, zero warmup, and one retained sample per emulator draw. Longer iterations and other controls remain options; warmup, retained-sample counts, and default controls adapt to the settings.

  • Default the installed reproduction script to the marginal oneiter500 profile; update the vignettes and recorded example to these defaults.

spDBL 1.1.0

  • Add optional RStan calibration with Gaussian discrepancy marginalization, coherent posterior recovery, equal pooling of emulator conditionals, and conditional-fit diagnostics.
  • Add a sigma2R option and complete metadata to the emulator wrapper.
  • Add an offline GP for predicting AR design rows without further PDE solves. Its interpolation uncertainty remains excluded from calibration.
  • Extend exact FFBS prediction with fixed coefficient trajectories, cached factors, and conditional covariance; preserve the default mean interface.
  • Correct sigma2R trajectory sampling to condition backward on sampled states.
  • Add compact calibration data, two package vignettes, and installed reproduction scripts. One-iteration runs are labeled execution experiments.
  • Show 500 one-transition calibration samples in the end-to-end vignette, with eta histograms and a variance/discrepancy/field comparison panel.
